title: A Star That's Also a Black Hole? Meet the 'Black Hole Star'
summary:
Have you ever looked up at the night sky and wondered what's really out there? Astronomers just found something so strange and new, it doesn't even have a name yet—they're calling it a 'black hole star.'

Using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope, scientists spotted a super bright red dot in the very early universe, just a few hundred million years after the Big Bang. At first, it looked like an enormous star, about the size of our whole solar system. But here's the twist: it's putting out 100 billion times more energy than any normal star can make. That's way too much for a regular star, which gets its power from nuclear fusion (like a giant space furnace). So what could it be?

The team, led by MIT scientist Rohan Naidu, thinks it's a mashup of a black hole and a star. Imagine a huge, dense cloud of gas shaped like a star, but with a black hole hiding in the middle. That black hole would be 100,000 times heavier than our sun! The gas around it glows super bright, making the whole thing look like a star on the outside.

This discovery might also explain other mysterious 'little red dots' that show up in almost every deep space picture from the telescope. Scientists have been arguing about what those dots are for years. Now, maybe they're all black hole stars!

The team wasn't even looking for this. They were searching for the oldest galaxies and found this red dot that was too red and too bright to ignore. One scientist compared the red color to how wildfire smoke can make the sun look red. But this wasn't smoke—it was something way cooler. So next time you see a red star, remember: it might not be a star at all!
why_it_matters: This matters because it shows that space still has big surprises, and new tools can change what we think we know about the universe.
